description:
Goal

A closure-call result refines the authoritative callable row forward: a genuinely grounded direct target uses that executable return contract, while opaque, escaping, ambiguous, or row-uncertain calls retain the public ValueRef contract. Interpreter, JIT, and AOT consume the same producer-owned call and return facts without boxing an exact result or hardcoding a reconstructed target.

Signal

On integration HEAD 2de30c10c, curried_add passes interp but run/build fail because an exact first closure target returns the inner closure as two capture lanes while every ClosureCall result is unconditionally labeled PublicCallableReturn. Main resumes one ValueRef and passes it to a specialized apply/2 input declaring two captures plus one surface argument, so native emits 2 arguments for 3 parameters.

The grounding prototype fixes curried_add across interp, run, build, and the built artifact, but exposes an upstream false singleton in enum_take_drop_split. Many reducer rows feed one shared recursive Function96 activation; its zero-lane callable input is pointwise-normalized to singleton Function205, whose zero-lane capture is similarly normalized to Function204. Grounding the return unlocks native direct-call lowering of that false target and JIT invokes take_while after false; interp remains correct through runtime closure identity. This is the correlated activation-row loss proven by fz-9i4.7.10.2, not a transport/native distinction.

Strategy

First complete fz-9i4.7.10.2 so activation inputs preserve correlated publisher rows and exact callable targets are authoritative. Then rebase and rerun this spike. If curried_add still requires return grounding, preserve the lowered producer as ClosureCallReturn { callsite, callee ValueId } and refine from the corrected settled callable row: a non-first-class singleton target aliases that exact ExecutableReturn for shape and callable-owner flow; every other row remains public. Keep durable RuntimeDemand and target-return product dependencies so replacement and withdrawal re-settle dependents. Do not change IncomingInputSlot, BackendCallArg, native encoding, or wrapper lookup; do not add adapters, padding, identity decoding, registries, provenance, sealing, passes, or fallbacks.

Plan

1. Wait for fz-9i4.7.10.2 to replace pointwise activation-input joins with correlated alternatives.
2. Rebase the spike and prove Function96/Function205 no longer publish false singleton targets; enum_take_drop_split must remain green through interp and JIT before any .4.5 promotion.
3. Revalidate grounded curried closure returns against their authoritative target ExecutableReturn and keep opaque, exact-first-class, and ambiguous calls public.
4. Pin repeated callers and same-session provisional-public to grounded replacement through durable product generations.
5. Verify curried_add and callable controls through interp, run, build, and built artifact, then full library, formatting, strict clippy, and docs.

Acceptance

After correlated-row repair, curried_add matches across interp, JIT, AOT, and the built artifact; enum_take_drop_split and the mapper-family correlation fixtures remain correct. Structural tests prove a grounded closure-call result and callable-owner facts alias the same authoritative row and ExecutableReturn; public/uncertain rows remain ValueRef; replacement and request order converge. The unconditional PublicCallableReturn origin concept is removed only when full gates prove no false target is exposed. No downstream compensation or duplicate callable authority is added.
title: Ground exact closure-call return transport
